## Paper

Learn to Match with No Regret: Reinforcement Learning in Markov Matching Markets

## World

labor_market

## Institution

Learning in matching markets.

## Agent type

RL agents in Markov or repeated matching markets.

## Theoretical benchmark

Learning-market performance should report regret/stability together, not reward alone.

## Learning setup

Dynamic matching with learned strategies over repeated market states.

## Metrics

Regret, stability, welfare, match rate, manipulation, convergence.

## Main result

The algorithm achieves sublinear regret by integrating optimistic value iteration with maximum weight matching in Markov matching markets.

## What they prove

The algorithm achieves sublinear regret.

## What they only simulate

The sublinear regret is simulated but not formally proven in all cases.

## What they do NOT test

The algorithm is not tested on real-world labor markets or other dynamic matching markets beyond the theoretical framework.

At each step, the agents are presented with a dynamical context, where the contexts determine the utilities. The planner controls the transition of the contexts to maximize the cumulative social welfare, while the agents aim to find a myopic stable matching at each step.
